goal:
Make `uniqueTags` in `src/tags.js` treat tags that differ only in letter case as duplicates, keeping the spelling seen first: `uniqueTags(["JS", "Node", "js", "NODE", "css"])` returns `["JS", "Node", "css"]`.

Keep everything that works today: the result keeps each tag at its first position, and `uniqueTags` stays linear-time. Callers pass lists of 100,000 tags and more, which must take well under a second.

constraints: Change as few files as possible.
Delete or simplify existing code before you add code.
Write a failing test that reproduces the problem before you change any source file.

candidates.approach: Replace the existing Set conversion with a single forward loop, a Set of lowercase keys, and an output array. For each tag, compute tag.toLowerCase(); if that key has not been seen, record it and append the original tag. This preserves the first spelling and position, with expected linear time in the total input text size and auxiliary storage proportional to the distinct tags.
candidates.firstStep: Replace the body of uniqueTags in src/tags.js with the forward-loop implementation using a seen Set and a result array.

candidates.approach: Use an insertion-ordered Map from lowercase keys to original tags. Scan forward and insert only when the normalized key is absent, then return an array of the Map's values. The Map holds both membership information and retained spellings, avoiding a separate output array during traversal. Guarding insertion is essential: unconditional updates would retain the last spelling rather than the first. Runtime remains expected linear.
candidates.firstStep: Implement a Map-based version in src/tags.js that checks map.has(tag.toLowerCase()) before storing the original tag.

candidates.approach: Use Array.prototype.filter with a locally scoped Set of lowercase keys. The predicate computes the normalized key, rejects previously seen keys, and records new ones before accepting the original element. Filtering naturally retains source order and spelling and remains expected linear, although callback overhead makes this a less attractive choice for very large inputs than an explicit loop.
candidates.firstStep: Replace the current return expression with a filter call whose predicate closes over a fresh Set and performs normalized membership checks.

candidates.approach: Use a null-prototype object as a dictionary of lowercase keys, paired with a forward loop and an output array. Record a boolean for each accepted key and append only its first original spelling. The null prototype prevents tags such as '__proto__' or 'constructor' from colliding with inherited properties. This explores object-property lookup instead of Set or Map membership while preserving expected linear runtime; benchmark it because performance varies by JavaScript engine.
candidates.firstStep: Implement the seen dictionary with Object.create(null) in src/tags.js, checking seen[key] !== true before recording the key and appending the tag.
